descriptionChirho: A masculine noun referring to a thin, flat cake or wafer, specifically an unleavened wafer used in sacrificial and consecration rituals. All three clusters represent the same culinary/ritual item differing only in number (singular vs plural construct) and prefixed conjunctions. Arabic رَقَائِقَ/رَقَاقَةً/رَقِيقَةَ (raqā'iqa/raqāqatan/raqīqata, all forms of 'thin wafer/flatbread'), Spanish hojuelas/hojuela/hojaldre ('wafers/wafer/puff pastry'), Hindi पूरी/पपड़ी/पतली रोटी (pūrī/papṛī/patlī roṭī, 'flatbread/crispy thin bread/thin bread'), Korean 전병/얇은 빵/얇은 과자 (jeonbyeong/yalbeun ppang/yalbeun gwaja, 'griddle cake/thin bread/thin cracker'), Swahili mikate myembamba/maandazi/mkate mwembamba ('thin breads/fried dough/thin bread'). Found in Exodus 29:2,23, Leviticus 2:4, 7:12, 8:26, Numbers 6:15,19 exclusively in Levitical offerings anointed with oil.
